Office or remote, as approved Travel: International travel based on program needs Position Summary The Senior Manager of International Programs is Cross International’s operational leader for its international program portfolio. Reporting to the International Programs Director, the Senior Manager translates the organization’s vision, current strategic plan, and approved program strategies into disciplined execution, clear staff accountabilities, strong partner relationships, timely donor deliverables, and measurable results. This is a hands-on working manager role in a lean department. The Senior Manager supervises program staff, assigns and balances portfolios, establishes operating rhythms, maintains the department’s master portfolio view, and coordinates program design, implementation, monitoring, budgets, field payments, grant procurement, compliance, and closeout. The Senior Manager is the first point of operational escalation and provides the Director with concise, decision-ready information on performance, risk, resources, and required action. The Senior Manager is also a cross-functional leader who collaborates with Development, Operations and Marcomm departments to align priorities, strengthen operational handoffs, and ensure accurate, timely program and partner information is available for organizational decision-making and reporting to the Board. The role champions the consistent adoption of organization-wide systems, processes, and data standards within Programs and contributes actively to continuous improvement, professional development, and a healthy, mission-aligned organizational culture. The Senior Manager also leads the Programs team’s operating workflow for major foundation and other institutional funding. Within the strategic and programmatic framework established by the Director, the Senior Manager coordinates go/no-go decisions; owns opportunity and deliverable calendars; prepares first drafts; synthesizes staff and partner input; manages compliance matrices and internal deadlines; and completes editing, assembly, correspondence, award documentation, amendments, renewals, closeouts, and narrative reporting. Portfolio owners supply implementation content, and the Director provides strategic direction and final executive programmatic review for major opportunities. Apply for this job Essential Functions The allocations below describe the expected emphasis of the role and may shift as organizational priorities evolve. Portfolio Operations and Team Leadership (35%) Translate approved program strategy into annual operating plans, quarterly priorities, portfolio assignments, staff workplans, milestones, and deadlines. Directly supervise, coach, and hold accountable assigned Programs staff. Lead weekly and monthly operating rhythms and maintain a reliable master portfolio dashboard covering program status, partner deliverables, grants, payments, procurement, results, and risks. Balance workloads and decision rights across a lean team; establish cross-training, coverage, escalation thresholds, and practical systems that reduce single-person dependency. Conduct regular performance and risk reviews, document corrective actions, and escalate concerns to the Director. Program Cycle, Partner Relationships, and Field Implementation (25%) Oversee the full program cycle, including concept development, partner due diligence, agreements, implementation, monitoring, adaptation, transition, and closeout. Ensure each program has a clear owner, approved scope and budget, documented outcomes, implementation schedule and reporting requirements. Maintain structured communication and follow-up with ministry partners and coordinate field monitoring, technical support, partner capacity strengthening, safeguarding, and compliance action. Coordinate timely operational responses to implementation delays, emergencies, partner concerns, underperformance, and other field issues. Institutional Grants, Proposals, and Reporting (25%) Own the Programs team's workflow for major foundation support, including proposal and reporting calendars, go/no-go coordination, compliance requirements, review gates, and internal deadlines. Complete final editing, document assembly, submission preparation, routine foundation correspondence, grant files, award documentation, and final version control. Coordinate amendments, renewals, and closeouts and ensure final narrative reports are accurate, evidence-supported, internally approved, and submitted on time. Maintain grant compliance matrices and translate award requirements into program workplans, partner expectations, data needs, budgets, payment schedules, and reporting calendars. Ensure proposed commitments are feasible and aligned with approved program strategy; route major submissions to the Director for strategic direction and final executive programmatic review. Program Budgets, Field Payments, and Compliance (5%) Review the programmatic agreement, approved budget, and supporting documentation for field-payment requests before submitting complete approval packages to Finance. Approve ministry partner payments within delegated authority and resolve missing program or partner documentation. Monitor program budgets and in coordination with the Director to initiate timely forecasts, corrective action, and budget modifications in coordination with portfolio owners, partners and operations. Maintain complete program agreements, approval records, compliance checklists, payment and procurement files, and audit-ready documentation in the designated systems of record. Organizational Collaboration, Systems & Professional (10%) Partner with Development, Operations and Marcomm departments to align priorities, coordinate timelines, anticipate information needs, strengthen handoffs, and resolve cross-functional operational issues. Implement and reinforce organization-wide systems, processes, data standards, policies and internal controls within the Programs Department; support staff adoption and provide practical feedback to improve their effectiveness. Ensure accurate, timely, appropriately governed program, partner, financial, grant, risk and results information is maintained and available to authorized internal stakeholders for organizational decision-making and reporting to Executive Leadership and the Board. Participate actively in cross-departmental planning, organizational initiatives, staff meetings, retreats, and culture-building activities that strengthen collaboration, accountability, learning, and alignment with CI’s Christian mission and core principles. Maintain an intentional professional-development plan and dedicate regular time to relevant training, coaching, peer learning, and sector engagement; apply and share learning to strengthen individual team and organizational performance. Supervisory Scope and Decision Authority Directly supervises the International Programs Officer and other Programs staff as assigned. Manages hiring, onboarding, goal setting, portfolio assignment, coaching, performance feedback, development planning, and performance evaluation in coordination with the Director. Approves routine workplans, portfolio assignments, partner follow-up, program adjustments, and complete payment, procurement, and grant packages within formally delegated authority and established review requirements. Recommends major program, partner, institutional-funding commitments to the Director and escalates matters exceeding delegated financial, contractual, safeguarding, reputational, or strategic authority. Key Success Indicators The master portfolio system is current, program and partner deliverables are visible, deadlines are met, and material risks are escalated early with recommended action. Programs staff and ministry partners understand ownership, standards, deadlines, and escalation pathways and receive timely follow-up, support, and performance feedback. Ministry Partner Payments files are accurate, complete, timely, and audit-ready, with exceptions actively resolved. Major proposals, amendments, renewals, closeouts, and narrative reports are coherent, feasible, donor-ready, evidence-supported, and submitted on time. Program decisions and corrective actions use credible results and learning, and reported claims can be supported by documented evidence. The Director receives concise, decision-ready reporting on portfolio performance, staffing capacity, funding deliverables, operational bottlenecks, and material risks. Bachelor's degree in international development, nonprofit management, public administration, agriculture, public health, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. At least eight years of progressively responsible experience in international development, humanitarian assistance, or comparable ministry programs, including at least three years supervising staff or leading a multi-country or multi-partner portfolio. Work Environment And Other Requirements Work is performed primarily in an office or approved remote setting and requires sustained use of a computer, virtual collaboration tools, and frequent verbal and written communication.
